claims.action: The Western Capital had fallen. Zhamu failed to take Yingzhou and withdrew to camp north of the city. That night he sent Alubu with four hundred men to scout. The garrison sallied with three thousand in a surprise attack; Alubu met them on the road, took more than a hundred heads, and captured sixty horses.
claims.sourceText: 時已下西京，闍母攻應州未下，退營於州北十餘裏，夜遣阿魯補率兵四百伺敵，城中果出兵三千平襲，阿魯補道與之遇，斬首百余，獲馬六十。

claims.action: Liao appointed Muzong, Taizu, Cibushi, and Huandu each to the office of xiangwen.
claims.sourceText: 遼人命穆宗、太祖、辭不失、歡都俱為詳穩。

claims.action: When Cibushi stormed the stronghold of Wuchun and Womouhan he took Sanbin and Sada and their mother as well. He made her a secondary consort and raised the two boys.
claims.sourceText: 辭不失破烏春窩謀罕城，獲三濱、撒達，並獲其母，以為次室，撫其二子。

claims.action: Sagai and Cibushi meanwhile sent word in haste to the hunt.
claims.sourceText: 而撒改、辭不失使人告急於獵所。

claims.action: Sada warned that Azu'a would rebel. Cibushi disbelieved him and had him executed.
claims.sourceText: 撒達告阿注阿必為變，不信而殺之。

claims.description: Relay riding at a reported thousand li in a day

claims.derivation: Approximately derived from death in AD 1152 at stated age 53

claims.statement: Accepted the order to capture the Liao warrior.

claims.action: Egunai, Yehe's son, was a man of imposing stature.
claims.sourceText: 訛古乃，冶訶子，姿質魁偉。

claims.action: At fourteen he entered Prince of Qin Zonghan's army and often led the van as scout.
claims.sourceText: 年十四，隸秦王宗翰軍中，常領兵行前為偵候。

claims.action: When the main army struck at the Liao emperor, Egunai took sixty armored riders, ran down the Liao Pacification Commissioner Tushan, and captured him. With seven riders he overtook the Liao princess Yabulai and presented her as a prize.
claims.sourceText: 及大軍襲遼主，訛古乃以甲騎六十，追遼招討徒山，獲之，又以七騎追獲遼公主牙不裏以獻。

claims.action: A Liao relief army drew up for battle. One man spurred out from the line. The commander said to Egunai: "Can you take him for me?"
claims.sourceText: 有軍來為遼援，方臨陣，中有躍馬而出者，軍帥謂之曰：「爾能為我取此乎？」
訛古乃曰：「諾。」

claims.action: He did, and brought him back alive. The man's name was Tonggua, reckoned among the bravest of the northern tribes.
claims.sourceText: 果生擒而還，問其名，曰同瓜，蓋北部中之勇者也。

claims.action: Egunai was famed for relay riding and could cover a thousand li in a day.
claims.sourceText: 訛古乃善馳驛，日能千里。

claims.action: On the campaigns against Song he was repeatedly sent on urgent dispatches.
claims.sourceText: 及伐宋，屢遣將命以行。

claims.action: In Tianhui 8, while with the Prince of Qin at Yan, he learned Yudu had rebelled in the northwest. The prince sent him by relay post. He left at dawn for Tiande and arrived before sunset.
claims.sourceText: 天會八年，從秦王在燕，聞余睹反于西北，秦王令訛古乃馳驛以往，訛古乃黎明走天德，及至，日未曛也。

claims.action: In Huangtong 1 his service won him the rank of General of Tranquil Reach and the governorship of the Dieci Tanggu tribe.
claims.sourceText: 皇統元年，以功授甯遠大將軍，迭刺唐古部節度使。

claims.action: In year 5 he received command of a thousand households.
claims.sourceText: 五年，授千戶。

claims.action: In year 6 he became Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit.
claims.sourceText: 六年，遷西北路招討使。

claims.action: In year 9 he was made prefect of Tiande and Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit.
claims.sourceText: 九年，再遷天德尹、西南路招討使。

claims.action: In Tiande 2 he was summoned to audience.
claims.sourceText: 天德二年，召見。

claims.action: In year 4 he became prefect of Lintao and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold-Purple Tally.
claims.sourceText: 四年，遷臨洮尹，加金紫光祿大夫。

claims.action: He died in office at fifty-three.
claims.sourceText: 卒官，年五十三。

claims.action: Yehe's sons were Alubu, Gunan, Egunai, and Sanda.
claims.sourceText: 冶訶子阿魯補、骨赧、訛古乃、散荅。

units.zh: 古者太史掌敘邦國之世次，辨其姓氏，別其昭穆，尚失。
units.en: Even in ancient times the Grand Historian who ordered the ages of the realms, sorted clan names, and marked senior from junior lines could not keep the record whole.
units.literal: In antiquity the Grand Historian kept the generations of the states, distinguished their surnames, and separated zhao from mu—and still there were lapses.

units.zh: 金人初起完毅十二部，其後皆以部為氏，史臣記錄有稱「宗室」者，有稱完顏者。
units.en: The Jin first gathered in the twelve Wanyi tribes, then took each tribe as a clan name. Court historians sometimes wrote "Imperial Clan", sometimes Wanyan.
units.literal: When the Jin people first arose in the twelve tribes of Wanyi, afterward all took their tribe as surname; in the historians' records some are called "Imperial Clan", some Wanyan.

units.zh: 稱完顏者亦有二焉，有同姓完顏，蓋疏族，若石土門、迪古乃是也；
units.en: "Wanyan" itself split two ways: same-surname Wanyan were really distant kin, men like Shitumen and Digunai;
units.literal: Those called Wanyan also fall into two kinds: same-surname Wanyan, who were in fact collateral kin—Shitumen and Digunai are examples;

units.zh: 有異姓完顏，蓋部人，若歡都是也。
units.en: different-surname Wanyan were really tribesmen, men like Huandu.
units.literal: and different-surname Wanyan, who were in fact men of the tribe—Huandu is an example.

units.zh: 大定以前稱「宗室」，明昌以後避睿宗諱稱「內族」，其實一而已，書名不書氏，其制如此。
units.en: Before Dading they were called "Imperial Clan"; after Mingchang, to avoid the taboo on Ruizong, "Inner Kin"—the same group in fact. Registers record personal names, not clan names; that was the rule.
units.literal: Before the Dading era they were called "Imperial Clan"; after Mingchang, to avoid the taboo on Ruizong they were called "Inner Kin"—in substance one and the same. The annals give personal names, not clan names; such was the rule.

units.zh: 宣宗詔宗室皆稱完顏，不復識別焉。
units.en: Emperor Xuanzong ordered that all imperial kin take the name Wanyan, and the old distinctions ceased.
units.literal: Emperor Xuanzong decreed that all of the imperial clan should be called Wanyan, and no further distinction was made.

units.zh: 大定、泰和之間，袒免以上親皆有屬籍，以敘授官，大功以上，薨卒輟朝，親親之道行焉。
units.en: From Dading through Taihe, relatives within tan-mian degree and nearer were entered in the clan rolls and ranked for appointment; when one within da-gong degree or nearer died, court paused in mourning—kinship was honored in deed.
units.literal: Between Dading and Taihe, kin within the degree of tan-mian mourning and closer all had household registers, by which offices were assigned; for kin within the degree of da-gong mourning and closer, death halted court audiences—the way of cherishing kin was practiced.

units.zh: 貞祐以後，譜牒散失，大概僅存，不可殫悉，今掇其可次第者著於篇。
units.en: After Zhenyou the pedigree books were lost; a broken outline alone remains, too fragmentary to exhaust. Here I collect what can still be sequenced and place it in these pages.
units.literal: After Zhenyou the genealogical registers were scattered and lost; only a rough outline survives, and it cannot be set forth in full. Now I gather what can be ordered by generation and set it down in this chapter.

units.zh: 其上無所系、下無所承者，不能盡錄也。
units.en: Lines that attach to nothing above and hand down to nothing below cannot be entered in full.
units.literal: Those with no tie above and no succession below cannot all be recorded.

units.literal: At right: sons of Ruizong—two in all, with Shizong.

units.zh: 右世宗子，與顯宗、衞紹王凡十人。
units.en: Listed at right: sons of Shizong—with Xianzong and Wei Shaowang, ten in all.
units.literal: At right: sons of Shizong—with Xianzong and Wei Shaowang, ten in all.

units.zh: 右顯宗子，與章宗、宣宗凡七人。
units.en: Listed at right: sons of Xianzong—with Zhangzong and Xuanzong, seven in all.
units.literal: At right: sons of Xianzong—with Zhangzong and Xuanzong, seven in all.

units.en: Listed at right: six sons of Zhangzong.
units.literal: At right: six sons of Zhangzong.

units.zh: 右紹王子，史稱六子，可以名見者四人。
units.en: Listed at right: sons of Shaowang; the histories say six sons, of whom four can be named in the record.
units.literal: At right: sons of Shaowang; the histories say six sons, of whom four can be named in the record.

units.zh: 右宣宗子，與末帝凡四人。
units.en: Listed at right: sons of Xuanzong—with the Last Emperor, four in all.
units.literal: At right: sons of Xuanzong—with the Last Emperor, four in all.

units.zh: 他書載守純子三人，可以名見者二人。
units.en: Other books record that Shouchun had three sons, of whom two can be named in the record.
units.literal: Other books record that Shouchun had three sons, of whom two can be named in the record.

units.en: Agunai (elder brother of the First Ancestor).
units.literal: Agunai (elder brother of the First Ancestor).

units.en: Hezhu (in Liao held Chen and Fu prefectures).
units.literal: Hezhu (in Liao held Chen and Fu prefectures).

units.en: Buhui (Military Commissioner of the Shuntian Army).
units.literal: Buhui (Military Commissioner of the Shuntian Army).

units.en: Baohuoli (younger brother of the First Ancestor).
units.literal: Baohuoli (younger brother of the First Ancestor).

units.zh: 迪古乃（同中書門下平章事。）
units.en: Digunai (Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).
units.literal: Digunai (Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).

units.zh: 婆盧火（安帝五代孫。泰州都統。）
units.en: Boluohuo (fifth-generation descendant of Emperor An; Commander-in-Chief of Taizhou).
units.literal: Boluohuo (fifth-generation descendant of Emperor An; Commander-in-Chief of Taizhou).

units.zh: 胡特孛山（婆盧火族兄弟。）
杲（本名撒離喝。行臺尚書、左丞相。）
units.en: Gao (born Saliehe; Mobile-Administration Minister of the Secretariat, Left Chancellor).
units.literal: Gao (born Saliehe; Mobile-Administration Minister of the Secretariat, Left Chancellor).

units.zh: 什古（昭祖曾孫。東京留守。）
units.en: Shigu (great-grandson of Zhao Zu; Eastern Capital Defender).
units.literal: Shigu (great-great-grandson of Zhao Zu; Eastern Capital Defender).

units.zh: 崇成（昭祖玄孫。武軍都指揮使。）
units.en: Chongcheng (great-great-grandson of Zhao Zu; Commander of the Martial Army).
units.literal: Chongcheng (great-great-great-grandson of Zhao Zu; Commander of the Martial Army).

units.zh: 冶訶（係出景祖。銀青光祿大夫。）
units.en: Yekhe (line traced to Jing Zu; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).
units.literal: Yekhe (line traced to Jing Zu; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).

units.en: Guhua (Military Commissioner of the Tiande Army).
units.literal: Guhua (Military Commissioner of the Tiande Army).

units.zh: 阿魯補（係出景祖。行臺左丞相。）
units.en: Alubu (line traced to Jing Zu; Mobile-Administration Left Chancellor).
units.literal: Alubu (line traced to Jing Zu; Mobile-Administration Left Chancellor).

units.en: Fang (Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs).
units.literal: Fang (Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs).

units.zh: 胡八魯（穆宗孫，寧州刺史。）
units.en: Hubalu (grandson of Muzong; Prefect of Ningzhou).
units.literal: Hubalu (grandson of Muzong; Prefect of Ningzhou).

units.en: Qi (Military Commissioner of the Lishe Army).
units.literal: Qi (Military Commissioner of the Lishe Army).

units.zh: 拔離速（宗室子。元帥左監軍。）
units.en: Balisu (imperial clansman; Marshal Left Supervisor of the Army).
units.literal: Balisu (imperial clansman; Marshal Left Supervisor of the Army).

units.zh: 銀术可（拔離族子。同中書門下平章事。）
units.en: Yinshuake (kinsman of the Balisu clan; Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).
units.literal: Yinshuake (kinsman of the Balisu clan; Fellow Associate Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery).

units.zh: 麻吉（銀术可弟。銀青光祿大夫。）
units.en: Maji (younger brother of Yinshuake; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).
units.literal: Maji (younger brother of Yinshuake; Silver Radiance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness).

units.zh: 宗賢（本名阿魯。太祖從姪。婆速路兵馬都緫管。）
units.en: Zongxian (born Alu; Taizu's nephew by the collateral line; Commander of the Bosu-route military).
units.literal: Zongxian (born Alu; Taizu's nephew by the collateral line; Commander of the Bosu-route military).

units.zh: 右諸宗室可譜者凡十一族，雖稱系出某帝，而不能世次，不譜於各帝之下，所以慎也。
units.en: Listed at right: of the imperial kin who can be entered in a pedigree, eleven clans in all; though they are said to stem from a given emperor, their generations cannot be fixed, so they are not entered under each emperor's line — hence the caution.
units.literal: At right: of the imperial kin who can be entered in a pedigree, eleven clans in all; though they are said to stem from a given emperor, their generations cannot be fixed, so they are not entered under each emperor's line — hence the caution.

units.zh: 時已下西京，闍母攻應州未下，退營於州北十餘裏，夜遣阿魯補率兵四百伺敵，城中果出兵三千平襲，阿魯補道與之遇，斬首百余，獲馬六十。
units.en: The Western Capital had fallen. Zhamu failed to take Yingzhou and withdrew to camp north of the city. That night he sent Alubu with four hundred men to scout. The garrison sallied with three thousand in a surprise attack; Alubu met them on the road, took more than a hundred heads, and captured sixty horses.
units.literal: The Western Capital had already been taken; Zhamu attacked Yingzhou without success, withdrew and encamped more than ten li north of the city, and by night sent Alubu with four hundred men to watch the enemy; the city indeed sent out three thousand in a surprise attack; Alubu met them on the road, beheaded more than a hundred, and seized sixty horses.

units.zh: 遼人命穆宗、太祖、辭不失、歡都俱為詳穩。
units.en: Liao appointed Muzong, Taizu, Cibushi, and Huandu each to the office of xiangwen.
units.literal: The Liao appointed Muzong, Taizu, Cibushi, and Huandu all as xiangwen.

units.zh: 辭不失破烏春窩謀罕城，獲三濱、撒達，並獲其母，以為次室，撫其二子。
units.en: When Cibushi stormed the stronghold of Wuchun and Womouhan he took Sanbin and Sada and their mother as well. He made her a secondary consort and raised the two boys.
units.literal: Cibushi captured the city of Wuchun and Womouhan, took Sanbin and Sada, and also took their mother, making her a secondary wife and nurturing the two sons.

units.zh: 而撒改、辭不失使人告急於獵所。
units.en: Sagai and Cibushi meanwhile sent word in haste to the hunt.
units.literal: Meanwhile Sagai and Cibushi sent men to report the emergency at the hunting grounds.

units.zh: 撒達告阿注阿必為變，不信而殺之。
units.en: Sada warned that Azu'a would rebel. Cibushi disbelieved him and had him executed.
units.literal: Sada warned that Azu'a would surely rebel; Cibushi did not believe it and killed him.

units.zh: 列傳第六 ○歡都子 謀演 冶訶子 阿魯補 骨赧 訛古乃 蒲查
units.en: Biographies 6: Huandu and his son Mouyan; Yehe and his sons Alubu, Gunan, and Egunai; Sanda's son Pucha
units.literal: Biographies 6: Huandu and his son Mouyan; Yehe and his sons Alubu, Gunan, and Egunai; Sanda's son Pucha

units.zh: 年十四，隸秦王宗翰軍中，常領兵行前為偵候。
units.en: At fourteen he entered Prince of Qin Zonghan's army and often led the van as scout.
units.literal: At age fourteen he was attached to Prince of Qin Zonghan's army and often led troops ahead as scout.

units.zh: 皇統元年，以功授甯遠大將軍，迭刺唐古部節度使。
units.en: In Huangtong 1 his service won him the rank of General of Tranquil Reach and the governorship of the Dieci Tanggu tribe.
units.literal: In Huangtong year 1, for his merit he was made General of Tranquil Reach and military governor of the Dieci Tanggu tribe.

units.en: In year 5 he received command of a thousand households.
units.literal: In year 5 he was granted command of a thousand households.

units.en: In year 6 he became Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit.
units.literal: In year 6 he was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit.

units.zh: 九年，再遷天德尹、西南路招討使。
units.en: In year 9 he was made prefect of Tiande and Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit.
units.literal: In year 9 he was again transferred to prefect of Tiande and Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit.

units.zh: 四年，遷臨洮尹，加金紫光祿大夫。
units.en: In year 4 he became prefect of Lintao and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold-Purple Tally.
units.literal: In year 4 he was transferred to prefect of Lintao and made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold-Purple Tally.

units.zh: 訛古乃善馳驛，日能千里。
units.en: Egunai was famed for relay riding and could cover a thousand li in a day.
units.literal: Egunai was skilled at relay riding and could cover a thousand li in a day.

units.en: He died in office at fifty-three.
units.literal: He died in office at age fifty-three.

units.zh: 訛古乃，冶訶子，姿質魁偉。
units.en: Egunai, Yehe's son, was a man of imposing stature.
units.literal: Egunai was Yehe's son, imposing in stature and bearing.

units.zh: 及大軍襲遼主，訛古乃以甲騎六十，追遼招討徒山，獲之，又以七騎追獲遼公主牙不裏以獻。
units.en: When the main army struck at the Liao emperor, Egunai took sixty armored riders, ran down the Liao Pacification Commissioner Tushan, and captured him. With seven riders he overtook the Liao princess Yabulai and presented her as a prize.
units.literal: When the great army struck at the Liao emperor, Egunai with sixty armored horsemen pursued Liao Pacification Commissioner Tushan and captured him; with seven horsemen he also pursued and captured the Liao princess Yabulai and presented her.

units.zh: 有軍來為遼援，方臨陣，中有躍馬而出者，軍帥謂之曰：「爾能為我取此乎？」
units.en: A Liao relief army drew up for battle. One man spurred out from the line. The commander said to Egunai: "Can you take him for me?"
units.literal: An army came as Liao relief; as the battle lines were forming, one man leaped his horse forth from the ranks; the army commander said to him: "Can you take this man for me?"

units.zh: 果生擒而還，問其名，曰同瓜，蓋北部中之勇者也。
units.en: He did, and brought him back alive. The man's name was Tonggua, reckoned among the bravest of the northern tribes.
units.literal: He indeed captured him alive and returned; asked his name, he said Tonggua—among the northern tribes a man of valor.

units.en: On the campaigns against Song he was repeatedly sent on urgent dispatches.
units.literal: When Song was attacked, he was repeatedly sent on urgent missions.

units.zh: 天會八年，從秦王在燕，聞余睹反于西北，秦王令訛古乃馳驛以往，訛古乃黎明走天德，及至，日未曛也。
units.en: In Tianhui 8, while with the Prince of Qin at Yan, he learned Yudu had rebelled in the northwest. The prince sent him by relay post. He left at dawn for Tiande and arrived before sunset.
units.literal: In Tianhui year 8, following the Prince of Qin at Yan, he heard Yudu had rebelled in the northwest; the prince ordered Egunai to ride relay post thither; Egunai set out at dawn for Tiande, and when he arrived the sun had not yet set.

units.en: In Tiande 2 he was summoned to audience.
units.literal: In Tiande year 2 he was summoned to audience.

units.zh: 冶訶子阿魯補、骨赧、訛古乃、散荅。
units.en: Yehe's sons were Alubu, Gunan, Egunai, and Sanda.
units.literal: Yehe's sons were Alubu, Gunan, Egunai, and Sanda.
